Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

ATG

A weak quarter on the only line that matters to ATG's owners: Swedish net gaming revenue fell 7.1% and parent EBIT 11.4%, dressed up by a 45% surge in Denmark that contributes almost no profit. The V85 experiment is being unwound (V75 returns 28 Nov) with NPS at -16, opex rose while revenue fell, and liquidity headroom is thin (SEK 15m / ~$1.5m undrawn) heading into a Q4 of restructuring charges. Cash generation (Q3 OCF SEK 499m / ~$50.2m) and 0.4x net bank debt/EBITDA keep this a sound credit; the open question is whether the incoming CEO can halt a four-year erosion in profit before owner transactions.

SEK 1,247m (~$125.5m)Net gaming revenue (Q3)-3.8% YoY / -4.2% QoQ
SEK 1,421m (~$143.0m)Total revenue (Q3)-3.1% YoY / -5.1% QoQ
SEK 392m (~$39.4m)Operating profit (EBIT, IFRS)-9.7% YoY; margin 27.6% (-200bps)

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Evolution AB

Evolution's Q3-26 delivered its first year-on-year revenue growth in five quarters (+3.7% to EUR 526.1m, ~$589m; est. +4.0% at constant currency) and held the adjusted EBITDA margin at 65.8%, but the quality is mixed: the ~30% of revenue in the Americas and Africa grew ~18% while the ~70% in Europe (-4.7%, share loss conceded) and Asia (+1.6%, cyber-crime unresolved) shrank ~1.5%. EUR 12.1m (~$13.6m) of one-offs pushed profit for the period down 3.6%, EPS growth is entirely buyback-driven, and Brazil's 5 October ban removes a growth engine from Q4. Stabilisation, not re-acceleration — with the FY26 ~66% margin target unchanged.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence high

Boyd Gaming Corporation

A "down 1%, up 2% underlying" quarter: revenue $990.5m (-1.4% YoY, ~1.1-1.3% below the ~$1.0bn consensus) and adj. EBITDAR $319.6m (-0.7%) were held up by Midwest & South (+2.5% adjusted), Online (+16%) and Managed (+13%), while the Las Vegas destination customer deteriorated further at the Orleans and Downtown (LV Locals EBITDAR -5%, Downtown -20%). Capital return of ~$180m and a 9.4% lower share count are doing the EPS work (adj. EPS $1.67, -2.9% YoY on adjusted earnings -12.6%), and leverage has drifted from 1.8x to 2.2x in two quarters as FanDuel-related tax payments, $650m of 2026 capex and $150m/qtr buybacks run ahead of cash generation.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

evoke plc

A revenue-only trading update that confirms the 2026 story: the estate shrink and a 1–2ppt bad-results hit took reported Q3 revenue down 7% to £406m (~$544m), while like-for-like constant-currency revenue fell 2% — a deceleration from +2% in H1 even with the July World Cup in the base. With no divisional, EBITDA or net-debt disclosure and no guidance during the offer period, the equity is now a bet on Bally's Intralot closing on time (headline 52p/~$0.70 all-share, shares ~42p/~$0.56) against a balance sheet already at 5.6x and drifting toward ~6x as the 40% RGD annualises.

Analyst report · Q3 2026 · Confidence medium

Svenska Spel

A revenue-steady, cost-heavy quarter. Group NGR rose 1.3% to SEK 1,898m (~$192m) as post-World Cup Oddset and casino (Sport & Casino +5.5%) plus Triss/Lotto offset a weaker Eurojackpot and a 14% Vegas decline, but a SEK 69m (+18%) step-up in external costs for the brand relaunch, AI and cloud migration cut operating profit 9% to SEK 656m (~$66m) and the margin by c.375bps to 34.6%. Net profit fell only 3% to SEK 565m (~$57m) because finance income tripled; the business is still well above the owner's 30% margin target, so the debate is about the duration of the spend, not demand.

Market report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Brazil

Brazil's regulated fixed-odds market delivered a record 9M 2026 on paper — R$11.12bn (~$2.19bn) of federal collections from gambling and betting (+55% YoY) and an estimated ~R$30bn (~$5.9bn) of licensed GGR — and then ceased to exist: MP 1.394/2026 (25 Sep) prohibited all sports betting and online gaming, extinguished all 87 authorisations without compensation and took every one of the 188 licensed brands offline on 6 Oct. With Lula re-elected on 25 Oct and the MP still in force, the only routes back are the STF (ADI 8027, public hearing 3 Nov) or Congress (initial deadline 23 Nov, realistically Feb 2027); the credible reopening case is a narrower, higher-taxed, ad-free re-regulation in 2027, not a return to the 2025 regime.

Market report · 2030 FORECAST · Confidence medium

Latin America

Latin America's 2030 story has split in two. The forecast houses still print a region of $51bn total GGR by 2030 (H2 Gambling Capital, Apr 2026) and $12.3bn of regulated online GGR by 2028 (Vixio), with a $467.6m online-poker niche (GVR) — but every one of those numbers pre-dates Brazil's MP 1.394/2026, which extinguished all 85 federal fixed-odds authorisations from 6 Oct 2026 and removed roughly half of the region's regulated online GGR (R$36.9bn / ~$7.2bn in 2025) at a stroke. Until Congress and the courts settle Brazil's fate, the investable regulated pool is Mexico, Colombia, Peru, Argentina's provinces and (eventually) Chile — a ~$5–7bn market with rising tax takes — while Brazilian demand migrates offshore.

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence high

Massachusetts

September 2026 was a tale of two channels: a labour strike at Encore Boston Harbor cut Massachusetts casino GGR 13.6% YoY to $82.69M (Encore -22.1%), while a hold-driven rebound lifted taxable sports wagering revenue 36.0% to $71.19M on handle that was actually 3.4% lower. Combined casino-plus-sports taxable revenue still edged up 4.0% to $153.88M and state tax 1.6% to $38.41M, but the real structural story of the month sits outside the MGC's remit — the Treasurer's two-month-old iLottery took $183M of online sales and the Legislature has shelved commercial iGaming until at least 2027-28, leaving a closed, duopoly-dominated sports market under a live 51%-tax threat as the only regulated online channel.

Market report · 9M 2026 · Confidence medium

Maine

Maine is a small, two-casino, tribal-exclusive-mobile market growing low-single-digits: 9M 2026 land-based GGR was $129.4m (+2.3%), carried entirely by slots (+4.5%) while tables fell 10%, and sports handle rose 10% to $450.2m with September hold normalising to 10.4%. The state keeps ~42% of casino GGR and 10% of sports AGR, and the only route to the online casino upside is through the Wabanaki Nations — whose iGaming bill (LD 1164) remains the single swing factor for the next 12-24 months.

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Connecticut

Connecticut's September 2026 data show a closed, three-licensee market that is still growing but visibly decelerating: record online-casino wagers of $1.95bn (+6% YoY) produced ~$57m of taxable GGR (+6% YoY, versus +17% in August), while sports handle rose 7% to $246.3m on an 8.9% hold and DraftKings overtook FanDuel in sports revenue. September was also the last month at the 18% iGaming tax — the statutory step-up to 20% took effect in October 2026 — so the state's take rises just as organic growth slows. For an outside operator the B2C door is shut by statute; the only realistic routes are B2B supply or displacing an incumbent partner at contract renewal.

Market report · JANUARY-SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence medium

Brazil

Brazil's regulated fixed-odds market was running at a record ~R$3.3–3.5bn (~$0.62–0.65bn) of monthly GGR and had already delivered R$11.1bn (~$2.07bn) of federal betting-and-lottery receipts in nine months when the Lula government switched it off: MP 1.394/2026 banned all sports betting and online gaming from 25 Sep 2026, forced platforms dark on 6 Oct and extinguished every authorisation on 25 Oct with no refund of the R$30m (~$5.6m) fee. January–September 2026 is therefore the high-water mark of a 21-month regulated experiment; whether a legal market returns — and in what shape — now rests on STF Justice Fux and a Congress that must act before the measure lapses around March 2027.

Market report · AUGUST 2026 · Confidence medium

United States

A flat headline hides a sharp mix shift: August 2026 US commercial GGR slipped 0.6% YoY to $6.48bn as sports betting revenue fell 15.6% to $1.00bn on a 160bp hold collapse (9.2% vs 10.8%) and handle that is now shrinking in every month without a World Cup, while iGaming (+12.3% to $1.03bn) out-earned sportsbooks for the month and retail casino held steady (+0.9%). For an operator, the regulated US sportsbook is now a share-and-tax fight against an untaxed, federally-sheltered prediction-market competitor whose legal status is heading to the Supreme Court; iGaming remains the growth vertical but is locked in seven states with no new launches in 2026.

Market report · Q2 2026 · Confidence medium

Cyprus

Cyprus's licensed betting market posted its strongest quarter in the NBA's published series in Q2 2026: GGR +23.6% YoY to €46.9m (~$53.4m) on stakes of €329.8m (~$375.8m, +10.6%), a series-high 14.2% hold, and online (Class B) now 64% of GGR. The regime is narrow (sports betting only; online casino, slots and exchanges prohibited), fiscally stable (15% of GGR all-in; 19 licensees unchanged for six quarters) and tightening at the edges — B2B supplier licensing, retail self-exclusion and social-media advertising enforcement are the live files, tax is not. For an operator the prize is a c.€120m-a-year online GGR pool contested by 13 incumbents; for a technology supplier the coming B2B licence is the more consequential change.

Market report · SEPTEMBER 2026 · Confidence high

Pennsylvania

Pennsylvania's September 2026 print ($555.0m, +4.1% YoY) confirms a $7bn-a-year, online-led market: iGaming (+6.8%) and a hold-driven sports betting rebound (+50% taxable revenue on −6% handle) carried a −3.2% retail casino month. The numbers are strong but the rules are tightening — a bipartisan online consumer-protection push (HB 2879, PGCB Regulation 125-258), the post-Supreme Court skill-game shake-out and unlicensed sweepstakes/prediction-market competition define the 2027 agenda far more than tax risk does.
